corrected_value.title: Attention please: Evaluative priming effects in a valent/non-valent categorisation task (reply to Werner & Rothermund, 2013)
corrected_value.title_o: Attention please: Evaluative priming effects in a valent/non-valent categorisation task (reply to Werner & Rothermund, 2013)

decisions.reason: Shipped row 713 and blind Target 0 both identify Reference 4, Spruyt (2013 online / 2014 print, DOI 10.1080/02699931.2013.832653), 'Attention please: Evaluative priming effects in a valent/non-valent categorisation task (reply to Werner & Rothermund, 2013)'. The competing match flag occurred because the blind coder also listed Werner & Rothermund (2013) [7] as Target 1; row 713 pairs directly with Target 0 (Spruyt [4]), the closest study in the replication chain whose materials, procedures, and positive evaluative priming effect are directly re-tested here after controlling for strategic processes.

decisions.quote: In line with both claims, research conducted at our lab revealed that the evaluative priming effect replicates in the valent/non-valent categorization task. This research was criticized, however, because non-automatic, strategic processes may have contributed to the emergence of this effect. We now report the results of a replication study in which the operation of non-automatic, strategic processes was controlled for. A clear-cut evaluative priming effect emerged, thus supporting initial claims concerning feature-specific attention allocation and dimensional overlap.
decisions.reason: Both shipped row 713 and blind Target 0 code the outcome for Spruyt [4] as 'successful'. Spruyt [4] reported clear-cut evaluative priming effects in the valent/non-valent categorization task, and the present replication confirmed a reliable evaluative priming effect (F(1, 76) = 6.42, p = .01) when non-automatic strategic processes were controlled for.

decisions.reason: Both shipped and blind coding classify the record as a 'replication'. The authors collected new experimental data from 78 undergraduate participants to re-test the published evaluative priming finding of Spruyt [4].
